summary: A public user-posted TikTok video reportedly shows two separate phones, each running ChatGPT Advanced Voice Mode, responding to the same human speaker in one conversational environment. Both assistants reportedly responded to the shared human input rather than visibly yielding to one another or following a coordinated turn-taking process.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The user reports two voice assistants responding to one human utterance in the same conversational setting without yielding. That report engages shared conversational-floor coordination. Sampled frames establish two co-located devices, but do not establish the spoken sequence, intended turn ownership or whether parallel replies were explicitly supported by the setup. The evidence therefore does not establish either a material loss of required turn coordination or demonstrated coherent allocation and recovery. The outcome is Boundary. This does not establish a missing internal arbitration component or a product-wide defect.

boundary_adjudication.material_engagement: The source reports two synthetic voice participants replying to a shared human prompt in one conversational setting. The reported competing responses concern allocation of the current conversational floor, rather than merely a wrong answer from one assistant.

unresolved_conditions.condition: Coherent continuation requires coordination of speaker identity, active-turn state, turn completion, yielding, or next-speaker allocation.
unresolved_conditions.assessment: The report describes one conversational setting, but the full setup and intended turn ownership are unavailable. It does not settle whether sequential allocation or explicitly parallel independent replies were required.

unresolved_conditions.condition: One or more synthetic participants fail to recognise or act on the relevant shared turn state.
unresolved_conditions.assessment: Not yielding is reported, but without the full exchange or intended turn allocation this does not independently distinguish disregarded turn ownership from intended parallel participation. No internal component defect is inferred.

unresolved_conditions.condition: The failure produces repeated answers, simultaneous or colliding responses, inappropriate interruption, inappropriate silence, or another material conversational-floor coordination breakdown.
unresolved_conditions.assessment: Colliding replies are attributed to the user report. Sampled frames cannot establish their timing, material interference or whether the reported behaviour violates the intended conversational allocation.

unresolved_conditions.condition: They use sufficient shared speaker and turn state for coherent allocation, yielding, handoff or bounded collision recovery.
unresolved_conditions.assessment: The report describes competing replies rather than a demonstrated allocation, yield, handoff or bounded recovery. The complete exchange has not been reviewed, so no protective coordination finding is established.

unresolved_conditions.condition: The observed exchange and coordination state demonstrate the intended turn ownership, including any explicitly agreed parallel participation.
unresolved_conditions.assessment: No inspected full audiovisual sequence or setup record demonstrates the intended turn ownership or an explicit agreement for parallel participation. Hidden coordination telemetry is not required; the relevant missing evidence is observable setup and exchange.

boundary_adjudication.decisive_blocker: The available report and sampled frames do not establish intended turn ownership, the complete spoken sequence or whether simultaneous output was intentionally supported by the interaction design. The intentional-parallel exclusion is unresolved, not established. Neither loss of required coordination nor demonstrated coherent coordination is established.
boundary_adjudication.resolution_requirements: An authenticated full exchange with its setup instructions could resolve intended allocation, yielding and collision recovery. No claim about an absent internal arbitration mechanism is necessary. Until such material evidence is available, retain this bounded disposition.

assessment_boundaries: The occurrence remains based on a public user report and is not treated as a platform-wide prevalence finding.
The complete audiovisual interaction has not been independently reconstructed; VIGIL does not infer undocumented timing or networking mechanisms.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The preserved user report describes two ChatGPT Advanced Voice Mode instances on separate devices responding to the same human input in one conversational environment. The record supports the bounded multi-participant observation but does not independently establish full timing, latency or platform-internal coordination state. Fresh sampled-frame inspection confirms the visible two-phone setting; it does not independently verify the reported spoken responses or their temporal overlap.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The reported competing replies engage conversational-floor coordination. The outcome is Boundary because intended allocation and the complete spoken sequence are not established by the inspected evidence. The user’s account of interference remains preserved. Two functioning assistants may interfere in a shared setting, but co-location alone does not prove lost turn state or an absent internal control. Intentionally supported parallel participation would be outside this finding. Harm remains the separately assessed low-confidence reported local interference. No relevant canonical external requirement has been established; the empty assessment list does not establish that all standards are irrelevant.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident shows why multi-agent safety cannot be reduced to the quality of each model response. Where several synthetic participants can observe one human input, the execution fabric needs explicit participant identity, floor ownership, yielding and conflict-resolution semantics.
